analysis_scope.sampling_notes: The checkout is shallow with depth 50, so history beyond the available sample may be truncated. Only one commit is visible. All 50 tracked paths and all documentation were inventoried; representative files from each major runtime component were inspected, but every line of the approximately 8,300-line implementation was not reviewed.

stated_purpose: Provide Chrome/Edge and iOS browsing clients that intercept pop-ups, redirects, cross-site navigations, and script-driven navigations so users can explicitly choose Stay or Go.

observed_capabilities.statement: The Chromium application is a Manifest V3 extension that injects interception code at document start in both MAIN and isolated execution worlds across HTTP(S) frames.

The Chromium runtime implements policy-controlled handling for anchor clicks, form submissions, window.open, location changes, programmatic clicks and submissions, settings persistence, custom or native prompts, diagnostic logging, and a 15-second post-Stay rollback guard.

The iOS target implements a SwiftUI multi-tab WKWebView browser with an address/search bar, navigation controls, onboarding, quick controls, settings, native navigation prompts, JavaScript hooks, and WebKit delegate interception.

Both clients support enable/disable state, cross-site or all-navigation modes, allowlist and always-prompt rules, a one-time bypass, a five-minute pause, script-without-gesture protection, and debug logging.
The iOS source includes a 15-second rollback guard even though the iOS specification's implementation-status section still lists that guard as unimplemented.

planned_work.statement: The Chromium MVP tracker calls for validating seven stories covering scaffold, policy, interception, controls, domain rules, hardening, cross-browser QA, and packaging; every completion checkbox remains unchecked.
The manual QA document calls for Chrome and Edge verification of eleven navigation, rule, bypass, script-guard, and diagnostic scenarios, but no results are recorded.

The iOS specification identifies further hardening and product work including dark-mode review, localization, accessibility auditing, iPad testing, history, and bookmarks, although parts of its implementation-status list are stale relative to source.

architecture.statement: The Chromium extension separates page-context prototype hooks, isolated-world DOM interception and modal presentation, shared policy modules, and a background service worker connected through CustomEvents and chrome.runtime messages.
The Chromium background worker owns chrome.storage.local settings, capped diagnostic logs, webNavigation observation, message handling, and tab-level rollback state.

The iOS target combines WKNavigationDelegate, WKUIDelegate, and WKScriptMessageHandler interception with SwiftUI views, a SettingsStore backed by UserDefaults, and JSONL diagnostic files in the app's Documents directory.

Four UMD JavaScript modules for constants, domain handling, storage normalization, and policy evaluation are byte-identical between the Chromium shared directory and the iOS bundle; iOS evaluates them through JavaScriptCore.

accomplishments.statement: The initial commit delivers substantive implementations for two platforms rather than only specifications or generated scaffolding.
The shared policy engine has deterministic precedence for disabled, paused, one-time bypass, URL validity, domain rules, script gesture protection, mode, and same-site decisions.
All 13 available Node tests passed locally, covering major policy branches, rule precedence, script-gesture handling, domain helpers, and settings defaults.
Both platforms include user controls and diagnostic facilities alongside the interception logic, including log export and clearing.

gaps.statement: The only automated tests exercise Chromium-compatible policy, domain, and settings modules; there are no automated interception, modal, background-worker, browser integration, Swift, or iOS UI tests.
The manual Chrome and Edge QA matrix is entirely blank, and no checked-in evidence demonstrates that either browser client or the iOS application has been built and exercised end to end.
There is no CI, release packaging, deployment automation, or published artifact evidence.

Documentation is already inconsistent with implementation: the iOS status section says rollback and favicons are absent while source implements both, and it describes a shared WKProcessPool while TabManager creates configurations without assigning one.
The visible history contains only one initial commit, so ongoing maintenance patterns and the evolution of design decisions cannot be assessed.

risks.statement: Diagnostic records can contain source and destination URLs, navigation metadata, and script context; persistent storage and export of these records may expose sensitive browsing information if logs are shared or retained unexpectedly.
The fixed list of twelve multi-part public suffixes is not a full public-suffix implementation, so some domains may be classified incorrectly as same-site or cross-site.
Broad HTTP(S) host access, page-prototype patching, fail-open behavior, and heuristic goBack rollback create compatibility and enforcement risks that require real-site testing.
Unchecked planning documents and stale implementation-status notes can obscure which acceptance criteria are actually complete.

suggested_next_actions.statement: Run and record the existing manual matrix on current Chrome and Edge releases, then add equivalent iOS simulator and device scenarios before treating the primary workflow as functional.
Add CI for the Node suite and automated coverage for content interception, background messaging, one-time-token consumption, rollback behavior, and the iOS policy bridge.
Reconcile the specifications and architecture notes with the current source, especially rollback, favicon support, WKProcessPool sharing, test coverage, and remaining MVP status.
Define a browsing-data privacy policy for diagnostics, redact URL query and fragment data where feasible, and make persistent logging and export behavior explicit to users.
Evaluate a maintained public-suffix implementation or document the limited suffix model and add tests for unsupported country-code and private suffixes.

questions: Is the iOS browser intended to be a co-equal product, an experimental port, or a validation environment for the extension policy?
Have Chrome, Edge, simulator, or physical-device tests been performed outside the repository, and should their results be recorded?
What browsing-data retention and redaction guarantees should apply to diagnostic URLs and script metadata?
Should the repository remain an incubating private prototype, or is store/release packaging an intended near-term outcome?
Is shared cookie and session state across iOS tabs required, given that the documented shared WKProcessPool is not configured in TabManager?

No credential-like tracked filenames were identified. The ignore file covers common Xcode artifacts but does not contain explicit .env or credential-file patterns; no secret values were accessed.
The shallow checkout exposes a single commit, d03c4ae, dated 2026-07-11 and titled Initial commit; no local tags or additional branches are present.

confidence.rationale: Primary source, manifests, specifications, and a passing policy test suite establish a substantive dual-platform prototype. Confidence is limited by the absence of browser and iOS build evidence, completed manual QA, integration tests, CI, releases, and accessible live GitHub verification; documentation also contains stale implementation claims.

limitations: The shallow depth-50 checkout may omit older history, although only one commit is visible.
No browser session or writable build environment was used, so the Chromium extension and iOS application were not executed end to end.
The iOS Xcode target was inspected statically but not compiled.
The GitHub API was unreachable, so supplied issue and pull-request metadata could not be refreshed and archival or release state could not be verified.
Credential safety inspection was limited to filenames and repository structure; no secret-file values were read.
